clue.text: Bag containing yellow sock lay abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned suggests something wild and unrestrained, so the letters of the two words run free into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone has carelessly left a sock lying about, and it ends up in a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' scrambles SOCK LAY into the answer; the definition is a playful description of the sac holding an egg's yolk.
explanation.definitionFit: The sac in an embryo holds the yolk, which is yellow, so it is literally a bag holding yellow.

clue.text: Did rabbit fly after ox?

indicators.note: after places the insect's name behind the animal's in the answer

parts.note: a yak is a long-haired Tibetan ox
a ked is a wingless fly that lives on sheep

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether a rabbit took flight behind an ox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rabbit' is British slang for talk on and on (from rhyming slang 'rabbit and pork'), so 'Did rabbit' is past-tense chattering, not a bunny.
explanation.definitionFit: To rabbit is British slang for chattering, and yakked is slang for having chattered.

clue.text: Lover of Shakespeare learning drama AMEN holds something unknown

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Lover of Shakespeare learning drama AMEN holds something unknown': LORE + NO round Z fits, but 'AMEN' is OCR debris with no role and the scan is blank, so the printed clue cannot be confirmed
annotationWithheld.clue: Lover of Shakespeare learning drama AMEN holds something unknown

clue.text: Hit men: one coming after you

parts.note: a hit is a success, as of a show or song
OR, other ranks, is the military abbreviation for ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A gangland warning that hired killers are on the way for you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit men' reads as contract killers, but it splits into two pieces; OR (other ranks) is a standard crossword shorthand for soldiers who are not officers.
explanation.definitionFit: A successor is the person who follows another into a role, so one coming after you.

clue.text: Poor compensation as farm's out of work

indicators.note: out of says one word is removed from the title of the work, leaving the rest standing

parts.note: Cold Comfort Farm is Stella Gibbons's 1932 comic novel, a literary work
taken as written, its apostrophe-s read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A farm worker laid off is given only a meagre payout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' is a book title here: Stella Gibbons's novel Cold Comfort Farm. Take FARM 'out of' it and the remaining two words are the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means consolation that hardly consoles, which is poor compensation for a loss.

clue.text: Eccentric one following female in city

parts.note: a card is an eccentric or amusing person
I is the Roman numeral one
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: An odd character trails a woman around town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' looks like a positional instruction, but it is the abbreviation F (as in 'pp. 4f'). CARDIFF is the capital of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardiff is the Welsh capital, a city in its own right.

clue.text: Acrylic covers produce tears

indicators.note: covers says the word Acrylic holds the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: Synthetic fabric covers are made, and somebody weeps.
explanation.definitionFit: To cry is to shed tears, so it means produce tears.

clue.text: Puzzle over cost of joining up

parts.note: re means about or concerning, a sense of over

indicators.note: in a down clue up says the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a sub, short for subscription, is the fee for joining a club

explanation.surface: Someone is puzzled about the price of a membership fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the joining fee because this is a down clue, read from the bottom; 'over' gives RE, the memo word meaning concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebus is a picture puzzle in which images or letters stand for words.

clue.text: African names common in Wales and Scotland, as English would have them

parts.note: Ivor is a familiar Welsh boy's name

parts.words: Scotland, as English would have them
parts.note: Ian is the anglicised spelling of the Scottish name Iain, just as Ivor anglicises Welsh Ifor

explanation.surface: A remark about how the English spell Celtic first names.
explanation.walkthrough: IVOR and IAN are the English spellings of Welsh Ifor and Scottish Iain, which is why the clue adds 'as English would have them'.
explanation.definitionFit: An Ivorian is a native of the Ivory Coast (Côte d'Ivoire) in West Africa.

clue.text: One would have left home for Casablanca

definitions.text: One would have left home for Casablanca

parts.words: One would have left home for Casablanca
parts.note: reads like an emigrant bound for Morocco, but Casablanca is the 1942 film, so this is someone going out to the pictures

explanation.surface: An emigrant sets off from home bound for Morocco.
explanation.walkthrough: Casablanca is both a Moroccan city and the classic Bogart film; the traveller is only going to the cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who leaves the house to see a picture like Casablanca is a cinema patron.

clue.text: Ship's captain caught with a woman leaving a Scottish town

parts.note: Captain Kirk commands the starship Enterprise in Star Trek
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: leaving says the second a departs from the word for a woman

parts.note: a lady is a woman

explanation.surface: A captain is caught with a woman who walks out on him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes the A out of LADY to give LDY. KIRKCALDY is a town in Fife on the Firth of Forth.
explanation.definitionFit: Kirkcaldy is a coastal town in Fife, Scotland.

clue.text: Regularly burn crude stew

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the word burn

parts.note: crude is unrefined oil

explanation.surface: A cook repeatedly burns a rough stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes alternate letters of 'burn', B and R. 'Stew' is a verb here: to swelter or seethe.
explanation.definitionFit: To broil is to swelter in great heat, as one stews in the sun.

clue.text: Name given to selector before touring province

indicators.note: touring says the first word travels round the second

parts.note: ere is an old word meaning before
NI, Northern Ireland, is often called the Province

explanation.surface: A selector is named ahead of a tour of a province.
explanation.walkthrough: ERNIE (Electronic Random Number Indicator Equipment) is the machine that picks winning UK Premium Bond numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: The machine that draws British Premium Bond winners is known by this name.

clue.text: Estimate going round house with partner entertaining

indicators.note: going round says the estimate encircles the house

parts.note: costing is an estimate of price

explanation.surface: Someone works out the cost of a house while socialising with a partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosting jointly with someone else is entertaining alongside a partner.

clue.text: A drier's hers, when working

indicators.note: working suggests the letters being put to use and rearranged

explanation.surface: The salon's hair drier belongs to her while she is at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when working' scrambles A DRIER'S HERS into the answer, and the whole clue describes her: the salon drier is hers while she works.
explanation.definitionFit: A stylist who works in a salon uses a hair drier as a tool of the trade.

clue.text: Condition of cap worn by servant?

definitions.text: Condition of cap worn by servant?

parts.words: Condition of cap worn by servant?
parts.note: suggests a maid's uniform cap getting shabby, but the cap is the kneecap, worn down by kneeling to scrub

explanation.surface: A question about the state of a maid's uniform headgear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cap' means kneecap and 'worn' means abraded: the bursitis from long kneeling at work was named after maids who scrubbed floors.
explanation.definitionFit: This is prepatellar bursitis, an inflamed knee from prolonged kneeling, as when scrubbing floors.

clue.text: Time for workers to become better off Check tod (4,5) 09015 6221

definitions.text: Time for workers to become better off

parts.words: Time for workers to become better off
parts.note: reads like a pay rise making staff wealthier, but it is time off work given to recover from illness

explanation.surface: A union demand that workers should be more prosperous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better off' looks like richer, but it splits as 'better' (recovered) and 'off' (away from work).
explanation.definitionFit: Paid absence while ill is time away from work in which to recover.

clue.text: City in ruins built as new

indicators.note: in ruins says the letters are wrecked and rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A city lies in ruins, though built as a new one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in ruins' scrambles BUILT AS plus N into the Turkish city.
explanation.definitionFit: Istanbul is Turkey's largest city, formerly Constantinople.

clue.text: Producers count reels perfect current material

indicators.note: reels means staggers, so the letters lurch into a new order

explanation.surface: Film producers count reels of footage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reels' looks like film spools but is the verb 'staggers', scrambling PRODUCERS COUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: A superconducting material carries electric current with zero resistance, a perfect conductor.

clue.text: Old man getting whack with hose

parts.note: pop is a familiar word for father, one's old man
to sock is to hit hard

explanation.surface: Dad gets thumped with a garden hose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hose' means stockings here, not a garden hose. A popsock is a knee-high nylon stocking.
explanation.definitionFit: Hose means stockings, and a popsock is a short knee-length stocking.

clue.text: Offensive alumnus put on some act

parts.note: OB, old boy, is a former pupil
a scene is a part of an act in a play

explanation.surface: A former student performs part of a play.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene means indecent, grossly offensive to accepted standards.

clue.text: Collect third of margin inside footer

indicators.note: inside puts that letter within the word for the bill-footer

parts.note: one who foots the bill is a payer

indicators.note: third of picks the third letter of the word margin

explanation.surface: Someone collects a third of the profit margin from a footnote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collect' is a noun, stressed on the first syllable: a short prayer in the Anglican liturgy.
explanation.definitionFit: A collect is a short prayer read on a set day in Christian liturgy.

clue.text: Tip for ballet dancer in copy one put in post

indicators.note: in places the dancer's tip within the word for copy

parts.note: to ape is to copy
pointe is the tip of the toe on which a ballet dancer balances

explanation.surface: A ballet dancer passes on a tip to someone newly appointed.
explanation.walkthrough: Dancing 'en pointe' is balancing on the tips of the toes.
explanation.definitionFit: An appointee is someone who has been given a job, one put in a post.

clue.text: Time to abandon pretty fifties paradise

indicators.note: to abandon says the time letter leaves the word for pretty

parts.note: tidy, as in a tidy sum, means considerable, like pretty
L is the Roman numeral fifty, so two fifties are LL

explanation.surface: A nostalgic look back at the 1950s as a lost paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to abandon' removes T from TIDY to give IDY; 'fifties' is LL, not the decade.
explanation.definitionFit: An idyll is a blissful, peaceful scene, a kind of paradise.

clue.text: For him comparatively easy to drop a round?

definitions.text: For him comparatively easy to drop a round?

indicators.note: to drop says the round letter is removed

parts.note: looser is the comparative of loose, easy or relaxed
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone finds it easy to lose a round of a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping an O from LOOSER gives the answer, and the whole clue describes him: he drops rounds easily.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitual loser readily drops rounds in any contest.

clue.text: Not still sad about past? The opposite

indicators.note: about would put the sad word round the past one
The opposite reverses the stated containment, so the past word goes round the sad one

parts.note: by means past, as in walking by
low means sad or down

explanation.surface: Someone is gloomy about the past, or perhaps the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken literally, 'sad about past' puts the past word inside the sad one; 'The opposite' tells you to swap which piece is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Blowy weather is windy, the air anything but still.

clue.text: Frightful ogress may like Webster's material

indicators.note: frightful suggests a horrible mess, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A frightening ogress may resemble something from a gothic play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Webster' looks like the dramatist or the dictionary, but here is a web-spinner, a spider.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossamer is a spider's fine silk, so gossamery means like the web-spinner's thread.

clue.text: Upset Yank's stomach

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: a yank is a tug, a sharp pull

explanation.surface: An American's stomach is troubled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American, but it is a sharp pull.
explanation.definitionFit: The gut is the belly or stomach.

clue.text: Allowed to trap wolf almost in pond

indicators.note: to trap says the permitted word holds the wolf

parts.note: let means allowed

indicators.note: almost cuts the last letter from the wolf's name

parts.note: Akela is the wolf who leads the pack in Kipling's The Jungle Book

explanation.surface: Someone is permitted to trap a wolf that is nearly in a pond.
explanation.walkthrough: Akela, the wolf leading the pack in The Jungle Book, is also the title of a Cub Scout leader; 'almost' drops her last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A lakelet is a small lake, which is to say a pond.

clue.text: Creatures love being in shade, always (3-4) 22,984 Solutio

indicators.note: being in places the love letter inside the shade

parts.note: red is a shade or colour
O is love, a zero score in tennis
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A couple are always in the shadow of their love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love' is O, nil in tennis scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Roe deer are small Eurasian deer, living creatures.
